messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Idea for new theming system
parts:
Hi all,

I'm starting to think about a theming system that's easier to
customise, where you can easily specify the properties of all text
elements, all axis elements etc. Here's what I've come up with so
far:


theme <- list()

theme$text <- list(size = 12, family = "Helvetica", lineheight = 0.9,
vjust = 1, hjust = 0.5, angle = 0)
theme$title <- list(face = "bold")

theme$axis.text <- list(size = 10, colour = "grey50")
theme$axis.text.y <- list(angle = 0)
theme$axis.ticks <- list(colour = "grey50")
theme$axis.title <- list(vjust = 0.5)
theme$axis.title.y <- list(angle = 90)

theme$background <- list(fill = "white", colour = NA)

theme$legend.background <- list(colour = "white")
theme$legend.key <- list(fill = "grey95", colour = "white")
theme$legend.text <- list(size = 10)
theme$legend.tite <- list()

theme$strip.text <- list(size = 10)
theme$strip.text.y <- list(angle = -90)
theme$strip.background <- list(fill = "grey80", colour = NA)

theme$panel.background <- list(fill = "grey80", colour = NA)

theme$plot.title <- list(size = 14)

# Rename all components into alphabetical order
names(theme) <- sapply(strsplit(names(theme), ".", fixed = T), function(x) {
paste(sort(x), collapse = ".")
})

theme_find <- function(component) {
pieces <- sort(strsplit(component, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])

combs <- expand.grid(rep(list(c(T, F)), length(pieces)),
KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
combs <- unrowname(combs[order(rowSums(combs))[-1], ])
labels <- apply(combs, 1, function(x) paste(pieces[x], collapse = "."))

elements <- theme[intersect(labels, names(theme))]
Reduce(modifyList, elements)
}

theme_find("text.x.axis")
theme_find("text.y.axis")
theme_find("text.x.strip")
theme_find("text.y.strip")


Any thoughts or comments would be greatly appreciated.

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

messages.subject: Re: Idea for new theming system
parts:
Hi 

themeing system is a neat idea, I was developing theme system for my own interactive graphics, because sometimes I need that a change in theme would emit a signal to update a plot, I choose a reference class to represent the interactive system. but for ggplot2, I think a s3/s4 class or simple object might be enough, a theme object could be self-contained and have something like(the refernrence class API)

theme_bw$update(list(a = "b", c = 1:3)) : to update a element, then users could made their own them based on existing theme and store the object for future use. I may have a theme_new defined as 
theme_new <- theme_bw$update( a = b)

theme_bw$reset(): set to the prototype/default
theme_bw$find("a"): find a object a
theme_bw$show() : give a general graphic template for checking your theme and design?
theme_bw$apply(p): to apply a theme to a ggplot object, equivilant to p + theme, in this way, it may need to redefine "+", or need to simply add method to theme, so it works like p + theme$value(), or with a constructor like theme_bw().

This may require a theme to be self-contained object, and it knows what kind of theme it is with a prototype(like a reset help you reverse all the changes you made). 

we could have a top "Theme" VIRTUAL class,  all the sub-themes are class extends that with same method and elements are defined  as slots or fields for those class. 

it's just my random thoughts, maybe a simple list is enough in most cases.

cheers

Tengfei

messages.subject: Re: Idea for new theming system
parts:
I want to make sure I understand... It looks like items have multiple inheritance; they inherit properties from items that match between "." characters. That is, "axis.text.y" inherits from all of these when you use theme_find:
  "x", "text", "axis", "text.x", "axis.x", "axis.text", "axis.text.x"
Is my understanding correct?


Will there be a way for elements that don't have substring matches to inherit these properties? For example, "axis.title.y" inherits from "title", but not from "text":

> theme_find("axis.title.y")
$face
[1] "bold"
$vjust
[1] 0.5
$angle
[1] 90

I think there are two senses in which we use the word text. In one sense, it refers to all the text in the graphic. In another sense (specific to ggplot2), it refers to the "text" elements, like legend.text, axis.text, and so on., distinct from "title" elements. It would be nice to have a way of setting general text properties (i.e., the first sense) for a graphic.


Will there be default values for these properties? For example, suppose I make my own theme, and set:
  theme$text <- list(size = 12, family = "Helvetica")
In this case, I haven't defined lineheight, hjust, vjust, or angle. Will this cause problems?

One more note: there's a small typo with "theme$legend.tite".

-Winston

Ok, I am becoming greedy..... Themes could be derived from ggplot2 and developed to a single package(like scales) that all other static or interactive graphic system could benefit from(e.g. cranvas), so I will vote for reference system. and use objectSignals, objectProperties package, make all elements settings as properties...

so "Text" could be a reference class, extends a VIRTUAL "Theme_element", with fields size, family listed as properties.  we need to make constructors for every theme elements like Text(), Axis.text().... for simple use, or we could just use Text.gen$new(...) to return a object.

For even more complicated system, we can define some VIRTUAL class for telling the difference between a text in element or general text by using contain = "". ..., this may solve Winston's problem too. 

If this is too much, please ignore them :)

Tengfei
